approach.method_basis: The Parent is a graph-based genetic algorithm whose oracle calls are chosen by Gaussian-process Thompson sampling. Each round of ten, it breeds a fresh pool of 160 candidate molecules from a 64-molecule elite. Parents come mostly from the top score quantiles, and each offspring is made either by joining connected fragments of two parents, sometimes followed by one more edit, or by a short chain of atom, bond and ring edits. Duplicates are rejected, and so is any offspring that would add a sulfur environment its scored parents do not already contain. A Gaussian process trained on every molecule scored so far in the run, using count-based Morgan fingerprints and a Tanimoto-type similarity, scores the whole pool; ten correlated posterior samples each take their best remaining candidate, and those ten molecules are scored. On top of this the Parent has a stall reflex: after three rounds in a row without a new best score, only the forty pool members with the highest predicted mean may be picked, until a round improves again. Two separate random-number generators drive a run: one makes every breeding decision, the other draws only the posterior samples. The reflex itself uses no randomness and changes nothing until a run first stalls.
approach.novelty: This node adds no new search behaviour. It is a placebo that measures how far luck alone moves this Parent's scores when a whole run takes a different random path. At the start of every round, before any breeding, it draws one number from the breeding generator and throws it away, so later breeding decisions use different random draws while every rule, threshold and the selector's own random numbers stay exactly the same. The same placebo was run once before, but on the previous Parent, which had no stall reflex, and every reading on this Parent has borrowed that number. The siblings either changed a rule (a mixture of Gaussian processes, niche-based survivor retention, releasing or holding the stall restriction) or removed an unused mutation floor and reproduced the Parent byte for byte, so none of them measured departure alone. Because the reflex is silent until a run stalls, this node is forecast to retrace the earlier placebo exactly, up to the first stalled round in each run where the restriction changes a pick, and then to go its own way. On this path the reflex also fires in the two deco_hop runs that never stalled on the Parent. The result gives the Parent its own luck band and shows whether its two unusually lucky seed-0 results, on deco_hop and sitagliptin, survive a re-draw.

observed_bottleneck: Every reading on the formal Anchor n-61b9b3bfb40d still borrows its departure scale from a different Parent. The only law-free references were drawn on the mask-free n-1744a1494180: the ungated breeding re-draw n-1c2f17550a3e (panel -0.009888, cell SD 0.079364, band [-0.050871, +0.031095], median_2 band [-0.007767, +0.006695]) and the stall-gated allocator-stream controls n-47993ce5d053 (-0.001735) and n-843b25e73dee (+0.007747). The Anchor adds a stall reflex that restricts 88 of its 435 announced batches (29 episodes, 19 batches at restricted depth six or more, 13 of 15 sessions; a recount from its own trajectories reproduces its logged counter in 435 of 435 batches), and its +0.010577 gain over that Parent rests mainly on two sitagliptin_mpo cells. Its completed children (n-1c27fae8e61d -0.136643, n-e1a97c9e8713 -0.047213, n-c7eb0cb7da3b -0.007929, n-5911390da209 -0.000562, and the byte-identical reproduction n-cf8d309c06de at 0.000000) were all read against the borrowed band. The Anchor also carries two fragile high cells reached by single late jumps: deco_hop seed 0 jumps from 0.609560 to 0.856148 at evaluation 281 and was reproduced by none of the 35 ungated descendants of the previous Anchor (the earlier breeding re-draw ended at 0.611233); sitagliptin_mpo seed 0 jumps from 0.723499 to 0.765861 at evaluation 282 and is the highest of 220 recorded seed-0 cells on that task. Without an Anchor-local law-free panel, a stream-perturbing arm's loss on those cells, and any ungated panel delta on this Anchor, cannot be separated from path departure.
hypothesis: Law-free breeding-stream path divergence on the stall-masked Anchor. At the start of every announced batch, directly after the batch counter increments and before the inherited stall-state computation, the GP fit and the first breeding decision, draw exactly one value with random() from the Evolution's own seeded random.Random(seed) generator, which GraphOperators shares, and discard it. That generator drives quantile parent and rank sampling, the crossover-versus-mutation and finishing coins, walk length and every operator, site and element draw, so all later breeding decisions consume different pseudo-random words (Python's variable-word rejection sampling can absorb the offset inside one draw, which is why the identical discard on the mask-free Parent left the seed-1 sessions at batch 1 and the other ten at batch 2 or 3). No law changes: probabilities, operator menu and weights, continuation and escalation, crossover and finishing, the sulfur gate, identity admission, both duplicate scopes, greedy-64 retention, quantile breeding, the 160 pool target, the accepted-only count-Morgan GP, the K=3 / M=40 stall-time top-mean eligibility mask with its counter and restoration rule, and the correlated Thompson allocation with its separately seeded torch generator, whose standard-normal rows stay bitwise equal to the Anchor's. Because the Anchor's mask consumes no random numbers and acts only on restricted batches, the Child is exactly the earlier mask-free breeding re-draw plus this Anchor's mask: it retraces n-1c2f17550a3e record for record until each session's first restricted batch whose top-forty picks differ from that reference's, and is a new realization of the Anchor's own law thereafter. The claim is a measurement, not a gain: the complete matched panel delta against the Anchor is what law-free path departure costs on this Anchor, and its two fragile cells either survive the re-draw or do not.

finding_summary.headline: Luck-only re-draw on this Anchor cost -0.0205 exactly as forecast; both lucky seed-0 cells were lost, and its own luck band is [-0.0555, +0.0146]
finding_summary.insights:
Both of this Parent's high seed-0 cells belong to its particular path, not to its rules. A re-draw that changes no rule loses both, as every earlier arm that perturbed the pre-stall stream did. Any arm that leaves the Parent's early path therefore starts about 0.023 behind on the panel from those two cells alone, and departure by itself breaches the deco_hop must-preserve margin. The new band also moves the bar for gains. Its upper edge falls from +0.031 to +0.015, because this Parent's re-draw lands lower and its cells spread less. A median_2 task-mean change now needs to exceed about 0.014 either way to stand clear of path luck, nearly twice the borrowed width, because luck alone moved two median_2 cells by +0.014 and -0.015.

This reading and the borrowed one are two dependent views of one breeding re-draw, not two draws. They share 2,197 scored molecules and identical selector random numbers, so their widths must not be pooled into a variance estimate. One realization bounds the luck band; it does not estimate its distribution. The pairing with the earlier run differs only by the stall restriction and came out at almost exactly zero (+0.000013). So the restriction's +0.0106 gain on the Parent's own path did not appear on this one re-drawn path. That pairing is one coupled realization and prices nothing. Whether the restriction helps still needs trigger-matched evidence.

Method diagnosis, from this node's trajectories and the molecular report, in three parts. First, late search is decoration of an inherited core. Only 13.6% of the runs' total best-score gain came after evaluation 150, and the median late improvement was +0.002. In 6 of 15 runs more than half of the last 50 proposals share the scaffold of the run's best molecule. The molecular report describes one inherited aromatic core per run with substituents permuted on it. Second, the surrogate ranks well but its uncertainty is wrong in a task-dependent way. The eventual improvers sat at a median posterior-mean rank of 5 of 160, yet beat their predicted means by a median 1.4 posterior SDs, 69 of 255 by more than 3. Realized scores fell within one posterior SD for 96% of median_2 picks but only 20% of sitagliptin picks, and 334 of 870 sitagliptin picks landed more than 3 SDs below their mean. The Thompson draws therefore explore on a scale that is too wide on one task and far too narrow on another. Because the error runs in opposite directions, no single fixed noise or amplitude constant can correct it. A surrogate whose predictive uncertainty is calibrated online within each run could correct it, for example by fitting amplitude and noise or by using a heavy-tailed or recalibrated residual model. Third, there is an early path lottery. The two re-draws of deco_hop seed 0 share their first 92 molecules. Both began proposing molecules above 45 heavy atoms from evaluation 24. Their mean size passed 53 heavy atoms by evaluation 100, and their last 50 proposals averaged 68 and 79 heavy atoms of polyaromatic growth, with 103 and 269 invalid breeding attempts. The Parent's run stayed at 27-31 heavy atoms throughout. The cell's fate is set by a few early breeding draws. A proposal scheme with a size-aware acceptance envelope, or a search scheme that keeps several independent basins alive, would reduce that lottery.

By the route's own conditions no second draw or discard sweep follows, so this measurement route stops here. Still open: the band applies only to stream-perturbing whole-run arms, and mask-confined contrasts keep their trigger-matched references. This round's parallel arms are not in this brief, so reading them against the band is left to Curate.
finding_summary.results:
The placebo ran exactly as registered. Every one of the 15 runs drew and threw away one breeding random number at the start of each of its 29 rounds (435 in total). The discard was always the round's first logged step, and the round-1 values were the predicted ones for each seed. No rule moved. The selector's own random numbers matched the Parent's bit for bit in all 4,350 picks, and every pool held 160 candidates. The stall counter, the top-forty restriction, the model fits, the sulfur gate, the duplicate checks and the operator, crossover and finishing rates all conformed to the inherited rules. The picks also sat at the same places in the predicted-score and uncertainty rankings as the Parent's: shift statistics +0.44 and -0.17 against a bound of 3.26.

Every forecast made before the run held exactly. Each run copied the earlier luck-only run (the same placebo on the previous Parent, which had no stall reflex) molecule for molecule. It did so until the first stalled round in which the top-forty restriction changed a pick, and then went its own way. The predicted split round, the predicted first different molecule and the predicted number of displaced picks matched in all 15 runs. That gives 2,197 of 4,500 scored molecules identical to the earlier run, as forecast. Against the Parent itself, every run left the Parent's path at the predicted point: evaluation 11 on seed 1 and evaluations 21-32 on seeds 0 and 2. Only 2.2% of the molecules scored after that point also appear in the Parent's same run. The stall restriction now fired in all 15 runs, including the two deco_hop runs that never stalled on the Parent, from round 9 and round 18. In total it restricted 87 rounds in 28 episodes, against the Parent's 88 rounds in 29 episodes, with 13 rounds at depth six or more against 19.

Scores: the panel mean was 0.586579 against the Parent's 0.607030, a reference delta of -0.020452. Seed macros moved -0.0614, +0.0011 and -0.0011; 8 cells rose and 7 fell, with a cell SD of 0.0678. The registered value R4 would take if the restriction were neutral on this path was -0.020465. Neither lucky cell reproduced. Deco_hop seed 0 ended at 0.6077 instead of 0.8561. This run was level with the Parent through evaluation 280 (0.6077 against 0.6096) and never made the Parent's single jump at evaluation 281. Sitagliptin seed 0 ended at 0.6702 instead of 0.7659. This run stood at 0.5019 at evaluation 153 and reached 0.6702 at evaluation 211. By evaluation 153 the Parent was already at 0.6484, and it climbed to 0.7235 by evaluation 280 and 0.7659 at evaluation 282. Those two cells cost -0.0229, more than the whole panel loss; the other 13 cells average +0.0029. The cells in task order (zaleplon, deco_hop, drd2, median_2, sitagliptin) are: seed 0 +0.0061, -0.2485, +0.0169, +0.0140, -0.0956; seed 1 +0.0103, -0.0100, -0.0087, +0.0011, +0.0129; seed 2 -0.0349, -0.0132, +0.0196, -0.0151, +0.0383. Two cells, drd2 seed 2 and sitagliptin seed 1, ended exactly at their pre-departure floors.

The pre-registered reading rule gives this Parent its own luck band: -0.020452 with half-width 0.035031. An ungated whole-run panel on this Parent now stands above path luck only above +0.014579, and below it only under -0.055482. The borrowed band was -0.050871 to +0.031095. For median_2 the band is -0.000011 with half-width 0.013750, i.e. -0.013760 to +0.013739; the borrowed one was -0.007767 to +0.006695. Among the protected tasks, deco_hop fell 0.0905 (0.6168 against 0.7074), far beyond its 0.02 margin, and all of that loss comes from seed 0. Drd2_docking (+0.0093), sitagliptin (-0.0148) and zaleplon (-0.0062) stayed inside their margins. Median_2 was unchanged at 0.228819 against 0.228830, with cells +0.0140, +0.0011 and -0.0151. Against the earlier luck-only run, which differs from this one only by the stall restriction, the panel moved +0.000013, with 3 cells up, 9 down and 3 identical.

molecular.headline: Decoration-only output: one inherited aromatic core per cell, flat stereochemistry, and halogen-on-nitrogen bonds in the top scorers.
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the node proposed 870 molecules per objective (900 read, 10 of them the shared initial cohort) and every cell behaves the same way: it adopts the single best-scoring member of the initial cohort, keeps that ring skeleton, and spends the remaining budget permuting substituents on it. Ring and aromatic content are genuinely high - digest ring_closure_rate 0.970-0.991 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.962-0.983 on every objective - but the rings are inherited, not built: in the highest-scoring twenty molecules of a cell I usually count one to three distinct Murcko scaffolds, and the last fifty proposals of a session differ from each other only by which methyl, methoxy, or halogen sits where. Two representation-level absences hold everywhere: digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 and charged_rate is 0.0 on all five objectives, although most proposals on the three objectives with sp3-rich winners carry undefined sp3 centres, so the generator writes flat, neutral strings only. The recurring chemical liability is bonding between heteroatoms and halogens: N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, N-N and O-O appear not only in the tail but inside the best-scoring molecules of three objectives. The optimizer also keeps proposing one- and two-atom species mid-session ('C', 'Cl', 'S', 'C#C', 'FF', 'OO' all appear as numbered proposals), which are molecules no chemist would submit. As a measurement reference the cells leave the Anchor's path early, at evaluations 11-32, and from that point the chemistry of a cell is decided by which initial-cohort member it latched onto. The two cells the ticket flags are instructive as chemistry: in deco_hop seed 0 this node's cell drifted into very large polyaromatic poly-ester species (SMILES up to 197 characters, near 70 heavy atoms, QED collapsing toward 0.06) while the Anchor's cell stayed on a compact fused purine-like core, and in sitagliptin_mpo seed 0 the Anchor's cell carried aliphatic amine centres through most of its proposals whereas this node's cell carried almost none and instead pushed fluorine onto ring nitrogen.

per_task.generated_character: Small, flat, two-ring molecules: mean SMILES length 42.7, around 24 heavy atoms, roughly three rings of which about 2.8 are aromatic. Essentially the whole high-scoring set is a methyl/methoxy-substituted indole-2-carboxanilide, the skeleton of initial-cohort member COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC (0.3051, the best initial molecule). The best molecule, Cc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(N)c3ccccc3)cc2c(C=O)c1C at 0.4491, is that core with methoxy traded for methyl, an aldehyde added, and an extra nitrogen hung on the amide nitrogen. Digest halogen_rate is 0.9506, so almost every proposal carries a halogen, but it is a decorative halogen on nitrogen rather than on carbon.
liabilities: halogen bonded to amide nitrogen in several best molecules, e.g. N(Cl)Br and N(F)Cl terminals
hydrazide-type N-N bonds in the top set rather than ordinary secondary amides
sulfur substituted directly on the indole ring nitrogen in COc1c(C)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3ccccc3)n2S)c1C
one- and two-atom proposals spent mid-session ('Cl' at evaluation 206, 'BrBr' at 206, 'C#C' at 165)
a strained halogenated peroxide ring proposed as ClC1COO1
missing_features: no defined stereochemistry anywhere (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0)
almost no basic aliphatic amine centre, which this node's own winners on other objectives carry
no trifluoromethyl or other fluorinated carbon group; halogens sit on nitrogen instead
no nitrile, sulfone, or sulfonamide polar group among the top scorers
no alternative ring skeleton: the aromatic bicyclic is inherited from the initial cohort and never replaced
no saturated heterocycle attached to the aromatic core
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The span is 0.0 to 0.4491 with median 0.318. Everything above about 0.43 shares one scaffold, so the gradient is not rewarding scaffold search at all; it rewards trading methoxy for methyl on the benzo ring and adding small substituents to the carboxamide nitrogen. Twelve of the twelve best molecules come from two seeds and one core; the floor is occupied by bare fragments such as 'Cl' and 'BrBr' at score 0.0.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and least drug-like molecules of the five: mean SMILES length 74.9 and a maximum of 197, with the seed-0 cell growing into near-70-heavy-atom fused polyaromatics bearing several propanoate esters. The seed-2 cell instead converged on a compact fused tricyclic carrying an ethyl or isopropyl ester and an exocyclic imine, as in the best molecule C=NC(Nc1cc(F)c(F)c(C)n1)c1c2c(C(=O)OCC)c(c3c1OCOC3)CC2 at 0.6310. Ring content is high (ring_closure_rate 0.9724, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9713) but much of it in the large cell is simple benzo-fusion rather than a designed scaffold.
liabilities: very large grown species with collapsed drug-likeness, e.g. the near-70-heavy-atom poly-ester polyaromatic
exocyclic C=N-H imines as a load-bearing motif, which are hydrolytically fragile
repeated proposal of fragments at the score floor ('C#C', 'FBr', 'C#N', 'CN')
strained and odd ring closures in the fused cores of the top set, including three- and four-membered fusions
peroxide-type O-O linkages present in a quarter of the seed-2 proposals
missing_features: no sulfonyl or sulfonamide group anywhere in the high-scoring set
no ordinary secondary amide; the set reaches for esters and imines instead
no defined stereochemistry although the winners carry several sp3 centres
no basic nitrogen centre on the fused core
no controlled scaffold replacement: the cells either keep a core or grow it by fusion
no size discipline, so the reward for compactness visible in the scores is never exploited
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The objective has a hard floor at 0.5 - 'C#C', 'CN' and 'FBr' all score exactly 0.5 - so the usable range is 0.5 to 0.631 and the gradient is extremely shallow. Within it, compact fused tricyclics with one ester and a fluorinated aminopyridine beat the very large polyaromatics; the biggest molecules in the set do not sit at the top. The twelve best molecules all come from one seed and differ only in ester alkyl group, halogen, and whether the saturated ring carries NH, O, or S.

per_task.generated_character: The most recognisably medicinal set, and the only one where the score range is nearly exhausted: best 0.9971 against a worst of 0.0002. Molecules run 30-34 heavy atoms with around five rings, only about two of them aromatic, so sp3 content is high. The dominant motif is an aliphatic amine centre - pyrrolidine, azetidine, or a spiro-fused pair - tethered to a dichloro- or chlorofluoro-aryl and a benzisoxazole, as in C=C(N)CC(CC1CCCN1C12CCN1c1cc(Cl)cc(F)c12)c1cccc2o[nH]c12 at 0.9971. A second, cleaner family appears in seed 2: an N-methyl fused indoline carrying an azetidine and a chlorophenol, CN1c2cc(-c3cc(O)cc(Cl)c3)cc3c2C1C(C1(N2CCC2)CCCN1)C3CN at 0.9931. Digest halogen_rate 0.9851 and ring_closure_rate 0.9839.
liabilities: spiro- and ring-fused three- and four-membered nitrogen rings as the core amine, a strained and reactive choice
benzisoxazole written in the unusual o[nH] tautomeric form rather than the aromatic ring
halogen on nitrogen and N-N bonds in roughly a fifth of the seed-2 proposals
chloromethyl groups attached to carbon in a large fraction of the seed-1 proposals
small fragments still proposed late, e.g. CCc1cccc(Cl)c1 at 0.0026
missing_features: no declared stereochemistry at all, although nearly every top molecule has two or more sp3 centres
few six-membered saturated amines; the set reaches the same pharmacophore through strained small rings
no amide or sulfonamide linker in the winners, so only one linker chemistry is explored
no acidic or strongly solubilising group to balance the basic centre
no charged or protonated form written anywhere (charged_rate 0.0)
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The climb is from 0.0002 to 0.9971 and the gradient is unambiguous: molecules gain score as soon as the sulfonamide-bearing initial fragment is replaced by a protonatable aliphatic amine held two to three carbons from a halogenated aromatic. The worst molecules are exactly the initial aryl sulfonamides, e.g. COS(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.0002, and the whole top twelve carry an amine nitrogen plus at least one chlorine. Hydroxy or amino on the distal aryl is worth a little more than halogen alone.

per_task.generated_character: A narrow, surprisingly clean band of fused tricyclic lactams: about 31 heavy atoms, four to five rings with only about two aromatic, mean SMILES length 54.2, and the lowest halogen content of the five objectives (halogen_rate 0.1172). The repeated winner is an ethoxy-substituted dibenzoxazepine fused to an N,N'-dimethyl piperazine-2,5-dione, CCOc1ccc2c(c1C)N1CCN(C)C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C1c1ccccc1O2 at 0.2368; the seed-2 cell found a related quinoline-fused variant, CCCc1nc2ccccc2c2c1CC2N1CCCN2OC(=C1OCC)C(=O)CN(C)C2=O. These are the most drug-like-looking molecules of the run by eye, yet the ceiling is only 0.2368.
liabilities: hydrazine N-N and hydroxylamine-type N-O single bonds inside otherwise sensible lactams
bridged and spiro ring fusions that read as drawing artefacts rather than designed rings
single-atom proposals spent mid-session ('C' at evaluations 123 and 65, 'NNO' at 27)
aminal and N-O-C linkages in the seed-2 finals, e.g. N2OC(=C1OCC) motifs that would not survive water
missing_features: no sulfonamide group in any proposal, despite polar sulfur chemistry being untouched everywhere
no fused pyrazolo- or imidazo-pyrimidine heteroaromatic; the aromatic rings stay plain benzo or quinoline
no defined stereochemistry at the ring-fusion centres the molecules create
little halogen exploration at all on this objective (only about 12 percent of proposals carry one)
no basic amine on the winning tricyclic, although two thirds of proposals elsewhere in the same cells have one
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Span 0.0 to 0.2368 with median 0.196, so almost the entire proposal set sits within 0.04 of the best and the gradient is nearly flat. What little slope exists rewards an ethoxy or ethyl on the aromatic ring and keeping the fused diketopiperazine intact; swapping one amide carbonyl for a hydrazine-type N-N, as in CCOc1ccc2c(c1C)N1CCNN(C)C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C1c1ccccc1O2, costs almost nothing, which tells me the objective is barely discriminating here. The floor is single atoms: 'C' at 0.0.

per_task.generated_character: Heavily fluorinated xanthine-like fused heteroaromatics of about 26 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length 47.2, halogen_rate 0.9172. The best molecule, N=c1c2c(C#CCF)n(C3=CC(CF)C=C3O)cc2n(F)c(=O)n1CCF at 0.6702, is representative: an iminopurinone core whose fluorine count is reached by putting F directly on ring nitrogen and by monofluoromethyl arms, plus a fluoropropargyl group. The seed-1 cell held a methoxypyridine-substituted variant, COc1cccnc1-n1cc2c(c1C1=CC(F)(F)C1S)c(=N)n(C)c(=O)n2F, and the seed-2 cell a partially saturated hydantoin-like ring system.
liabilities: fluorine bonded directly to ring and amide nitrogen in the great majority of proposals, which is not a real motif
sulfur substituted on ring nitrogen, as in C1=CC(F)(S)C1F and n(S) variants
two-atom proposals such as 'FF', 'FS', and 'S' scored at zero mid-session
a bare peroxide 'OO' proposed as evaluation 297 of the final batch
aminal N-C(F)-N centres in the seed-2 family that would not be isolable
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl or aryl-CF3; gem-difluoro appears in at most about a seventh of one cell's proposals
no free primary amine or beta-amino amide motif on the scaffold
no defined stereochemistry despite most molecules carrying sp3 centres
no triazole or other stable five-membered N-heteroaromatic to carry the fluorinated arm
no saturated six-membered amine ring in the cell that scored highest
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Span is effectively 0 to 0.6702 with median 0.225, and score tracks fluorine count almost monotonically: the top twelve each carry three or more fluorines, and the generator buys them wherever it is cheapest, which is on nitrogen and on CH2F, not on carbon as a trifluoromethyl group. Score survives swapping C for S on a ring nitrogen (identical 0.6573 for three such variants), so the objective is reading composition and gross shape rather than a sensible substituent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Highest-scoring molecules on three objectives carry N-F, N-Cl or N-Br terminals, for example COc1c(C)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(c3ccccc3)N(Cl)Br)cc2c1C and N=c1c2c(C#CCF)n(C3=CC(CF)C=C3O)cc2n(F)c(=O)n1CCF, and two-atom proposals FF, NF, FS and BrBr appear as numbered evaluations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator forms bonds between halogens and nitrogen, oxygen, or sulfur, and does so inside its own best-scoring molecules rather than only in its tail.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Proposal admission needs a bond-plausibility rule that rejects halogen bonded to N, O, or S, and more generally heteroatom-heteroatom bonds outside a small allowed list, so that budget is not spent on species a chemist would discard on sight.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Where score rises with fluorine count, fluorine arrives as ring N-F and monofluoromethyl arms while gem-difluoro appears in at most a seventh of one cell and trifluoromethyl in none; sulfur similarly appears bonded to ring nitrogen, as in COc1c(C)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3ccccc3)n2S)c1C.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator buys heavy-atom composition the cheapest way the string allows instead of through real substituent groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation vocabulary should offer whole chemically standard substituent groups as single moves, so composition changes arrive attached to carbon in motifs that exist, rather than as lone atoms placed wherever a valence is free.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on all five objectives, yet the sp3-rich winners routinely contain two or more undefined stereocentres, for example C=C(N)CC(CC1CCCN1C12CCN1c1cc(Cl)cc(F)c12)c1cccc2o[nH]c12 and CCOc1ccc2c(c1C)N1CCN(C)C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C1c1ccccc1O2.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never writes stereochemistry, even when the molecules it proposes are full of sp3 centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation and its operators have no stereo channel at all; adding one would let the search distinguish diastereomers it currently proposes as a single flat string, and would make its output describable as a real compound.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest charged_rate is 0.0 on all five objectives across 4350 proposals, while the chemistry it does produce includes amine and lactam centres whose relevant form is often the protonated or deprotonated one.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no charged or ionisable species whatsoever.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Neither the initial cohort nor the operators can introduce a formal charge, so an entire region of ordinary chemical space is unreachable; the atom and group vocabulary would have to admit charged forms for the search to reach it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Fragments such as C, Cl, S, C#C, FF and OO appear as numbered mid- and late-session proposals on every objective, including OO at evaluation 297 of a final batch and C at evaluations 65 and 123.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator keeps proposing one- and two-atom species late in a session, so a measurable share of the budget goes to molecules that cannot score.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Operators that delete or fragment a parent are returning the remnant as a candidate with no size or connectivity floor; a minimum-heavy-atom admission check would convert those evaluations into usable ones.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the twelve best molecules of most cells I count one to three distinct Murcko scaffolds, and consecutive late proposals differ only by methyl, methoxy, ester alkyl, or halogen position, for example the C=NC(Nc1cc(F)c(F)cn1)c1cc(C(=O)OCC)c(F)c2c1NCCC2 family and the Cc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(N)c3ccccc3)cc2c(C=O)c1C family.
transferable_gaps.gap: Late search is decoration-only: the generator permutes substituents on a frozen inherited skeleton and almost never replaces a ring system.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The move set needs genuine scaffold-level operations, ring replacement or ring-system transplant between parents, because substituent moves alone cannot leave the basin set by whichever starting molecule happened to score best.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One cell reached SMILES length 197 and near seventy heavy atoms as fused polyaromatic poly-esters with QED near 0.06, while the best molecules in the same objective were about thirty heavy atoms, so the oversized direction was pursued against its own score evidence.
transferable_gaps.gap: When the generator does grow molecules it grows them without bound, producing oversized species whose drug-likeness collapses.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Growth operators need a size or simple property envelope on acceptance, so that fusion and chain extension stay in the range where the generator's own observations are better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the cells whose winners are sp3-rich, two thirds to four fifths of proposals contain a three- or four-membered ring, and the best molecules carry spiro- or ring-fused small nitrogen rings, for example Oc1cc(C(CCl)CC2CCCN2C23CCN2c2cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c23)c2[nH]oc2c1.
transferable_gaps.gap: Where saturated ring chemistry is rewarded, the generator reaches it through strained three- and four-membered and spiro-fused rings rather than the common five- and six-membered ones.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction is closing whatever is nearest rather than sampling ring sizes by how common they are in real molecules; weighting ring formation toward five- and six-membered closures would keep the same pharmacophore without the strain.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
